_meta.description: Override validation rules for Phase 3 (and Phase 5). The LLM agent reads and applies these before writing any override decision. Update here — no Python changes needed.
_meta.maintained_by: LLM agent — add new rules when a new class of bad override is discovered

rules.description: The gcp_sku_id must exist AND must cover the row's gcp_region. Use find-sku.sh to verify before writing an override. A SKU that exists in us-east4 but not in asia-south1 will produce $0 cost in that region — same silent failure as no SKU at all.
rules.how_to_check: Run: bash scripts/find-sku.sh "<gcp_service>" "<gcp_region>" and confirm the returned SKU ID matches what you plan to write. If find-sku.sh returns nothing, the SKU does not cover that region — use veto or find the correct regional SKU.
rules.on_fail: Use veto and document that no regional SKU was found.

rules.description: A row whose projection_note contains 'no GCP equivalent', 'no GCS equivalent', or 'no direct GCP equivalent' was intentionally left as passthrough by a static mapper because no real GCP service exists for it. Overriding it to strategy=map invents a false mapping.
rules.how_to_check: Read the row's projection_note from review_flags.md. If it contains any of the intentional-passthrough phrases, do NOT override.
rules.on_fail: Use veto, citing the intentional passthrough note.

rules.description: A sustained-performance AWS source (any non-t-family EC2: m5, c5, r6g, etc.) must never be mapped to a burstable GCP family (E2, T2A Arm). These families use CPU-credit billing — the customer's SLA changes silently. This is a binary-compatibility boundary, not a cost tradeoff.
rules.how_to_check: Look at the row's usage_type or instance_type. If it is NOT a t2/t3/t3a/t4g instance AND the gcp_sku_name starts with 'E2' or 'T2A Arm', reject.
rules.on_fail: Reject the override. Find a sustained GCP family (N2, N4, C3, etc.) for the source's workload type.

rules.description: unit_multiplier must be strictly greater than zero. GCP cost = usage × multiplier × rate. A zero or negative multiplier produces $0 GCP cost regardless of the rate — an invisible silent error in the final report.
rules.how_to_check: Confirm the value you plan to write is > 0.
rules.on_fail: Do not write the override. Determine the correct multiplier from the instance spec (vCPUs for core component, RAM GiB for ram component).

rules.description: The unit_multiplier must have the right physical dimension for its component: core → number of vCPUs (typically 1–192), ram → RAM in GiB (typically 0.5–24576). Cross-component errors (vCPU value in the ram row, or GB value in the core row) produce a projection that is orders-of-magnitude wrong.
rules.how_to_check: For core rows: multiplier should equal instance_vcpus from aws_li_catalog. For ram rows: multiplier should equal instance_ram_gb. Cross-reference the instance spec if unsure.
rules.on_fail: Correct the component assignment or the multiplier value before writing.

rules.description: Sanity check: vCPU multiplier > 512 or RAM multiplier > 8192 GB is unusual and likely a data-entry error (e.g. confusing instance count with vCPU count, or writing bytes instead of GiB). Flag in reason but do not auto-block — some bare-metal or HPC instances are genuinely large.
rules.how_to_check: If core multiplier > 512 or ram multiplier > 8192, double-check against the actual AWS instance spec before writing.
rules.on_fail: Write the override but include a note in reason: 'Verified against instance spec — confirmed correct.'

rules.description: The gcp_sku_id must belong to the gcp_service you are specifying. A Compute Engine SKU paired with gcp_service='Cloud SQL' will mismatch rate lookups and produce wrong pricing. The find-sku.sh output shows which service owns each SKU.
rules.how_to_check: The service in find-sku.sh output must match gcp_service in your override.
rules.on_fail: Correct gcp_service to match the SKU's actual service, or find the right SKU for the intended service.

rules.description: GCP SKU IDs follow the pattern XXXX-XXXX-XXXX (three 4-character hex groups). Any other format is not a real GCP SKU ID. Do not invent IDs — always get them from find-sku.sh or the bundled catalog.
rules.how_to_check: Verify the gcp_sku_id matches the regex: [0-9A-F]{4}-[0-9A-F]{4}-[0-9A-F]{4} (case-insensitive). If it doesn't, it is not a real SKU.
rules.on_fail: Run find-sku.sh to get a real SKU ID. Never write an invented one.

rules.description: Cloud SQL default edition is Enterprise (standard), not Enterprise Plus (~2x). The LLM may upgrade to Enterprise Plus ONLY with explicit CUR evidence that the source workload needs Plus-tier features (near-zero-downtime failover, Data Cache). When CUR gives no edition evidence, pick Enterprise (or price-closest) and stamp '[tier chosen by price-proximity — no CUR evidence of edition; confirm with customer]'.
rules.how_to_check: If gcp_sku_name or SKU description contains 'Enterprise Plus', verify that the source CUR line item has explicit evidence of Plus requirements (or ARM/C4A architecture requirement documented). Otherwise, reject the Plus pick.
rules.on_fail: Downgrade SKU to Cloud SQL Enterprise edition.
